Having air conditioning at home is a luxury that keeps people comfortable during the hottest months of the year, and it’s debated whether the AC should stay blasting or be turned off when people head to work during the day.

Some swear that turning off the AC when they’re gone for a few hours is the most energy-efficient, cost-saving method. Others say it’s better to leave it running continuously, preventing the system from straining to rapidly cool the house down after the home has gotten warmer throughout the day.

Three experts interviewed by The Associated Press agreed that setting the thermostat a few degrees higher than normal while you’re away is generally the best way to balance energy efficiency against comfort and humidity.

While turning an AC unit off for several hours and turning it back on can save money and energy compared to continuously running it, that approach can lead to mold problems in humid environments as well as wear and tear that can cause more frequent repairs. The equation can also vary depending on other factors including comfort level, AC unit type and building insulation.

Air conditioning strategies differ in humid or dry climates

According to the U.S. Department of Energy, adjusting your thermostat by 7-10 degrees Fahrenheit (4-6 degrees Celsius) for eight hours a day can save up to 10% a year on heating and cooling.

Experts say there are a lot of factors to consider when deciding what AC habits save the most energy and money.

“If you’re gone for like 15 minutes to go to the grocery store, you don’t get any gain" by turning off your AC, said Elizabeth Hewitt, professor and urban planning expert at Stony Brook University.

But as a general rule, “if you’re going for your work day, say for eight hours or so, you’ll almost always save more energy and money by turning things off," she said.

In some climates, however, turning off the AC might not be feasible, so residents can set back their AC a few degrees instead of blasting cold air all day.

In dry places like Arizona, you can let the home warm up more by raising the thermostat a few degrees higher. But in humid climates like Florida, air inside the home can become damp and harder to cool, and turning the AC off for long periods can increase the risk of mold since the system helps control indoor moisture.

Bumping up the thermostat by 1 degree Fahrenheit (0.6 degrees Celsius) yields about a 3% savings in cooling costs, said Patrick Phelan, mechanical engineering professor at Arizona State University.

Phelan also said leaving your AC off for hours and then turning it back on could lead to wear that results in more frequent repairs. That is because it can take AC systems 15 to 30 minutes after they are turned on to perform most efficiently.

How much energy and money you can save depends on the kind of home you live in, said Gregor Henze, an architectural engineering professor at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Homes built with heavy materials like concrete or brick hold in cool air longer, while older, draftier houses heat up faster. In less insulated homes, Henze said, it makes sense to adjust the thermostat even if you’re stepping out for just a few hours, because the indoor temperature can rise quickly.

Some AC units save more energy than others

Whether you have a window unit, a smart thermometer or central air could influence your savings.

Window units are generally less efficient because they’re installed in an open window, making it difficult to seal out hot air completely, said Hewitt. She added that spraying “cheap foam spray insulation in open windows or areas that are drafty is a really low-hanging fruit that doesn’t cost a lot of money and really helps retain the indoor temperature in your home.”

Phelan says smart thermostats are a handy tool to remove the mental burden of tinkering with your manual thermostat multiple times a day. Smart thermostats “learn” by monitoring the occupancy with a sensor and raise the temperature when no one is home to conserve energy and lower it when people return.

“If you’re going from just an ordinary manual thermostat to installing a smart one like a Nest, then you can expect something like 10% savings," said Phelan.

How to cool your home without air conditioning

Each expert said simple steps like blocking sunlight can go a long way in keeping homes cool.

Henze pointed to “time-honored strategies” such as opening windows at night when it’s cooler. In dry climates, that night air doesn’t add much moisture, but in humid regions it can bring in dampness the AC will later need to remove.

Hewitt added that closing your blinds can make a difference of several degrees.

Phelan also noted that some blinds are designed to reflect sunlight and said tinted window films are another option.

___

O'Malley is a former Associated Press reporter.

Madison Square Garden is reportedly abuzz with activity as preparations for the highly anticipated wedding of pop superstar Taylor Swift and NFL star Travis Kelce get underway.

The iconic New York venue is said to be transforming for the couple's celebrations, which are expected to commence today, Thursday 2 July.

Before her current romance with the Kansas City Chiefs tight end, Swift's romantic history included other prominent figures, some of whom famously inspired her chart-topping hits.

Here is a timeline of Swift’s previous relationships.

Joe Jonas

The Jonas Brother was Swift’s first high-profile celebrity relationship when they dated for around four months in 2008.

She revealed on the Ellen DeGeneres Show that he broke up with her during a 25-second phone call.

open image in gallery The Jonas Brother was Swift’s first high-profile celebrity relationship. ( FilmMagic )

She reportedly wrote the song Forever & Always about their split.

Taylor Lautner

Around a year later, Swift dated Twilight actor Taylor Lautner after they met on the set of the film Valentine’s Day, where they played a high school couple who were obsessed with each other.

Fans speculated that her song Back to December was about Lautner when the track was released nearly a year after they broke up.

John Mayer

The pop star was romantically linked with John Mayer for a few months in 2009 and 2010. The singer-songwriter was 12 years her senior.

The relationship led to her hit song Dear John from her Speak Now album.

open image in gallery John Mayer and Taylor Swift perform onstage during Z100's Jingle Ball 2009 at Madison Square Garden. ( Getty )

She sings: “Dear John, I see it all now it was wrong. Don’t you think 19 is too young to be played by your dark, twisted games?”

Jake Gyllenhaal

Swift dated actor Jake Gyllenhaal for a few months from late 2010 to January 2011. The Hollywood star said to have inspired the Red album, including the song All Too Well.

Swift released the original 10-minute version in 2021 along with a short film starring Sadie Sink and Dylan O’Brien.

Harry Styles

Former One Direction star Harry Styles was pictured with Swift on an autumnal walk around Central Park in New York.

They reportedly dated from 2012 until January 2013 and the songs Out Of The Woods and Style are thought to be about the English singer.

open image in gallery Harry Styles and Taylor Swift reportedly dated from 2012 until January 2013. ( PA )

Meanwhile, Styles’ solo song Two Ghosts, from his debut album, is believed to be about his relationship with Swift.

Calvin Harris

Swift went on to date Scottish DJ Calvin Harris for around 15 months, with rumours circulating after they were first photographed together in April 2015.

The music producer, real name Adam Richard Wiles, confirmed they had split in a June 2016 tweet where he said: “What remains is a huge amount of love and respect.”

Tom Hiddleston

Swift was linked with Loki actor Tom Hiddleston for a few months after her relationship with Harris, but reportedly ended their liaison in September 2016.

Joe Alwyn

Swift was then with London-based British actor Joe Alwyn for six years before they reportedly split up in April 2023, just weeks after the pop star embarked on her Eras world tour.

open image in gallery Taylor Swift and Joe Alwyn’s relationship is said to have inspired a number of love songs on her albums Lover, Folklore and Evermore, ( AFP/Getty )

The relationship is said to have inspired a number of love songs on her albums Lover, Folklore and Evermore, with the song London Boy reportedly about Alwyn.

Matty Healy

Swift was next seen with The 1975 lead singer Matty Healy.

The pair were photographed together a number of times, and Healy was seen at one of the Eras Tour gigs.

open image in gallery Healy was seen at one of Swift’s Eras Tour gigs. ( Getty )

They reportedly called it quits in June 2023.

Travis Kelce

The soon-to-be newlyweds began their relationship after the American football star revealed on his New Heights podcast that he wanted to date Swift after they failed to meet when she performed at Arrowhead Stadium – home of his NFL team the Kansas City Chiefs.

In September 2023, Swift made her first trip to watch Kelce play and was spotted sitting next to his mother, Donna.

Kelce appeared at one of Swift’s Eras Tour shows at London’s Wembley Stadium in June 2024, arriving on stage as she prepared to perform The Tortured Poets Department section of the gig.

open image in gallery Preparations are under way for Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding (Charlie Riedel/AP) ( AP )

Wearing a top hat and tails, he helped prepare her to sing I Can Do It With A Broken Heart.

The pair announced their engagement in a joint Instagram post in August 2025 with the caption: “Your English teacher and your gym teacher are getting married.”

Swift referenced Kelce in a number of songs in her latest album, The Life Of A Showgirl, including Opalite – which mentions his birth stone, opal.

The couple are expected to marry at Madison Square Garden in New York on Friday.

Ahead of the United States celebrating the 250th anniversary of its independence from Great Britain, President Donald Trump has turned Washington, DC into a labyrinth of fenced-off areas amid his myriad construction projects, a new report highlights.

The president’s numerous attempts to renovate the nation’s capital have made many of the top attractions inaccessible to many. At the Reflecting Pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial, soldiers now stand guard, The New York Times reported.

This came after Trump attempted to renovate the pool so that it would be blue, but it has since been plagued by an algae bloom. The president has blamed vandals for causing the pool to turn an almost neon green.

As a result, federal officials have essentially closed off access to the pool and it will likely stay closed ahead of the late-night fireworks planned this weekend for the Independence Day celebration.

The Trump administration has said that seven people have since been arrested and seven received federal citations related to supposed vandalism of the pool.

open image in gallery Visitor has to crane camera over fencing installed to keep the public away from the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, which has been beset by problems since Trump doled out a no-bid contract to fix it ( Getty )

open image in gallery An America 250 sign sits outside Lafayette Park near the White House, Tuesday, June 30, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson) ( AP )

Trump has threatened 10-year prison sentences for supposed vandalism of the pool.

But an official with the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia said no records of arrests or citations had been produced by the administration or law enforcement related to the pool and vandalism.

“He likes the idea that he will walk out on the stage with a giant presidential wand and end decades of Middle Eastern warfare or prehistorical algae that defies modern chemicals,” Tim O’Brien, a biographer of Trump, told The Times. “When that doesn’t happen he goes into convoluted and damaging narratives.”

In June, former Olympian cyclist David Hearn was arrested for destruction of property for reaching into the pool to touch the lining that had peeled.

“No normal federal law enforcement authority of either party would have ever dreamed of charging an American for touching the Reflecting Pool,” Norman Eisen, Hearn’s lawyer, said.

open image in gallery The Reflecting Pool next to the Lincoln Memorial remains largely fenced off. ( Getty )

White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers called Hearn a “deranged individual suffering from a severe case of Trump Derangement Syndrome.”

“Thanks to President Trump, the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is restored, crystal clear and reflecting beautifully ahead of America’s 250th birthday celebration,” she said.

Since then, numerous tourists have visited the pool, but do so with National Guard members watching them closely. This comes even as shards of the lining at the bottom of the pool remained visible underneath the surface of the pool.

But the pool is not the only area cordoned off. Lafayette Park, the park area across from the White House normally open to the public, is currently closed off after the Trump administration spent $17.4 million on a no-bid contract to renovate the park.

Despite the work being mostly done and fountains working again, two layers of fencing blocks off the park.

This also comes as Trump seeks to add a massive ballroom to the White House, even knocking down the East Wing of the White House to do so.

He also hopes to construct a 250-foot “victory arch.” A small scale mockup of the arch at the Great American State Fair was recently seen oozing out a yellow substance.

News.title: Russia ‘launched drones to spy on Britain’s nuclear sites’ during 15-month campaign
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The Kremlin orchestrated a major surveillance campaign on nuclear sites across Europe – including Britain – using drones launched from one of Russia’s shadow fleet tankers, experts believe.

The findings could bring to an end a two-year mystery that started when drones were spotted flying over four sensitive US military bases in the UK. Investigators believed they were being flown by live operators, but no launch sites were found.

Now, experts at the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), a London-based think tank, have discovered that HAV Dolphin, a Russian-crewed cargo vessel, was docked near Hull at the time. Another vessel, the Seasons 1 tanker, was also in the North Sea near Essex.

open image in gallery The drones were first spotted flying over four sensitive US military bases in the UK ( AFP/Getty )

Having tracked the HAV Dolphin’s movements, they say it is “highly likely” that Putin waged a drone campaign in Nato airspace across Europe between August 2024 and February 2026, as part of what they say is the “Kremlin’s wider unconventional war on Europe”.

The concerted surveillance campaign targeted nuclear sites in the UK, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, the researchers said.

And an analysis of 144 incidents in more than a dozen countries over an 18-month period concluded Russian intelligence had operated with “substantial impunity”, according to the report, first published by The Times.

It warns: “The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) campaign operated with substantial impunity across European airspace – representing both a series of tactical successes for the Kremlin and a strategic failure of allied air defence.”

In November 2024 drones were spotted over RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall, in Suffolk, RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and RAF Feltwell, in Norfolk.

open image in gallery Putin’s government is thought to be ‘highly likely’ behind the drone campaign in Nato airspace across Europe ( Reuters )

At the time four B-52 bombers were based in RAF Fairford as part of an American task force.

The drones were also heard buzzing above Lakenheath, where facilities were being built to house nuclear weapons.

The US has had military bases in the UK for more than 70 years.

The report’s authors said that Moscow’s success was because of the “basic strategic insight” that “Europe’s air-defence architecture was designed to detect and defeat conventional air threats operating in a recognisable battlespace” rather than drones.

They said vessels could have acted as a “network relay system”, with one or two deploying and recovering drones and a third providing intelligence to the drone and its operator.

HAV Dolphin, which sails under the flag of Antigua and Barbuda, is currently thought to be off the coast of Portugal.

open image in gallery Signs warning against flying drones are displayed next to Sizewell B nuclear power station ( Getty )

The UK’s former national security adviser Lord Ricketts told The Independent: “This is yet another wake up call on how exposed we are in the UK to the breathtaking pace of development in the threat from drones. The Defence Investment Plan promises new anti-drone systems. These reports show why this must be a top priority”

Senior research fellow at the defence think tank Rusi Dr Sidharth Kaushalsaid: “The threat is a real one, however it should be contextualised. In peacetime, the goal is likely disruption and surveillance, which are consequential but not catastrophic.”

He added that the UK had a “limited” capability to counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems, or drones, and there was “considerable room for growth”.

Earlier this week Keir Starmer unveiled the long-awaited defence investment plan (DIP), with a promise to increase defence spending by £15bn, and modernise the armed forces so they are prepared for drone attacks and the threat posed by Russia.

But the government is yet to spell out how almost a third of the blueprint will be funded, with a decision on where that £4.7bn will come from to be made at the Budget in the autumn. That will prove a headache for Sir Keir’s likely successor Andy Burnham, who was only briefed about the financial “black hole” on Tuesday.

Ministers also recently announced new laws designed to crack down on Russian interference in the UK, warning saboteurs that they face jail if they deliberately damage vital undersea internet cables around Britain.

Minister Baroness Lloyd said the UK’s message to Putin was simple: “We can see what you are doing and any interference will have serious consequences.”

News.title: British women’s Wimbledon hopes end with Katie Swan exit
News.content:
Katie Swan became the latest home player to exit Wimbledon after being beaten in straight sets by Madison Keys, as British interest in the women’s draw ended on day four of the Championships.

Against a player ranked 174 places above her who claimed her third Eastbourne title last month, Swan was always going to face a tall order to reach the third round. But she should take heart from how she fronted up to the hard-hitting American, whose ferocious forehand reached speeds of 80mph.

Not so long ago, Swan was ranked outside the top 1,000 and, blighted by back injuries, began contemplating an early retirement from tennis. The way she handled the free-swinging Keys, who was twice broken by the Brit in a topsy-turvy second set, could breathe new momentum into the 27-year-old’s career.

In truth, Swan’s 6-1, 6-4 was not a reflection of her industriousness, at times belying her world no 196 ranking against Keys. Last year’s Australian Open champion mixed power with precision but delivered an under-par performance by her lofty standards. Her ball toss was all over the place in the first set, but she mixed finesse with firepower in the crucial moments.

Despite showing more resolve in a rollercoaster of a second set - which at one point saw both players trade consecutive breaks - Swan will rue her missed opportunities. The Briton had eight break points in this match and only converted two of them, before netting a forehand at 4-4, paving the way for Keys to reach the finish line.

More to follow...

News.title: Britain’s Arthur Fery produces tenacious display fit for a princess
News.content:
Hello and welcome to coverage from Wimbledon as Arthur Fery plays Finnish qualifier Otto Virtanen.

Frey earned his place in the second round after beating Bosnian opponent Damir Dzumhur ‌3-6, 6-2, ​6-2, 6-1. The match ⁠was overshadowed by Fery being called dishonest by Dzumhur.

But Fery, one of 12 British wildcards, kept his cool and even used earplugs while Dzumhur complained to the umpire.

“It was expected, to be honest,” said Fery, who is through to the second round for a second straight year. “He does that with everyone. I guess I was just ready for it before the match. If it’s a let, it’s a let for everyone, right, it’s not just a let for him. Whether the point carries on or not, it’s the same for both of us.

“He obviously wants to make a problem with the umpire and then is trying to speak to me about it. But there is nothing to really speak about. Just trying to get the other player involved for no reason.”

Fery is now on the verge of breaking into the top 100 after also reaching the quarter-finals at Queen’s Club earlier this month.

The British No 3 is the higher-ranked player but Virtanen has also shone on grass this summer and knocked out fourth seed Ben Shelton in the biggest upset of the tournament so far.

“It’s a surprise, definitely,” said Fery. “But it’s an opportunity. He’s obviously a great grass-court player.”

Fery grew up five minutes from Wimbledon and would often visit the tournament as a child. He is the heir to an estimated £275m fortune thanks to his father, Loïc Fery, a hedge fund manager and president of Brittany-based Ligue 1 club FC Lorient.

News.title: Overrated kitchen appliances and taste test secrets: Xanthe Clay answers your questions
News.content:
Xanthe Clay has been a Telegraph food columnist for 27 years, and is also our resident taste tester. It’s her job to sample supermarket staples in search of best-in-class products, and those to avoid.

Xanthe’s recent reviews range from the stand-out chicken Kyivs for a Seventies-inspired supper, to the picnic food that’s worth a place in your shopping basket. You might also have spotted her on the new series of MasterChef as a guest critic, savouring scallops and racks of lamb.

I interviewed Xanthe for our Reader Ask series, where members of the Telegraph Recommended community get to quiz industry experts.

Xanthe on kitchen gadgets



How likely is it that expensive appliances will be better value than cheap ones?

Lynda, East of England

There’s the million dollar question. Or the £100 question, at least. My advice would be to think hard about whether you need that appliance or whether you can borrow one from someone to play with for a couple of weeks. Give it a go before you buy something that might end up in landfill.

Quality varies, but some of the appliances which are made for Lidl and Aldi can be absolutely great at bargain prices. Equally, it’s worth paying out for things like metal casing instead of plastic and decent-quality attachments, because they’re incredibly expensive to replace.

What’s one premium kitchen appliance that has genuinely changed the way you cook — and one that’s completely overrated?

Ella, North West

I would say that a real revolution came with the microplane graters, because they radically increase how much citrus zest you get in a dish.

In fact, you have to be quite careful with old recipes. They might say the grated zest of a lemon, but they’d have been doing it on a little box grater where half of the zest got stuck in the holes. If you’re working with a modern microplane, you will probably get twice as much zest in your dishes.

I also have a very whizzy oven at the moment called an Anova oven, which steams as well. It’s great when you want to preserve things in jars; it has an internal thermometer so I can probe my meat as it cooks, and it can ping me and let me know when my meat is cooked to perfection.

In terms of things that aren’t worth it, there’s a lot. For me, probably not a juicer. I have one, but I’ve used it once in the last three years to make some juice out of lovage leaves for a recipe I was testing. We know that juice is really just pure sugar and it’s not something we should be drinking that much of, so I wouldn’t bother with a juicer.

News.title: Harry Kane saves England’s World Cup... and Thomas Tuchel’s job
News.content:
No [Kane has not surpassed expectation], that’s what we expect from him, I think it’s what he expects from himself. Difficult matches, close matches, Harry’s here to decide them, he’s top level.

[Impact of Anthony Gordon and the substitutes] Like I said the whole tournament, the energy and the team spirit is one the highest level and the commitment from everyone [shows], I think everyone fully understands what part of the tournament we’re in at the moment and what it really takes. If you could see the level of support coming on to the pitch but also from the players that are not selected, that don’t even get minutes, they keep pushing and pushing, you see the faces, they’re positive in the water breaks, that’s what it takes.

I think everyone feels very comfortable when he [Gordon] plays, everyone feels comfortable when he’s selected to finish the match because of the atmosphere that the team provides for each other.

Of course, we want it to be easy and have the first goal, but if you come back from 1-0 down, if you need the last quarter of the match to be strong, these are the experiences that give you genuine belief. You don’t need a manager to tell you because you’ve felt it. And now they’ve felt it and now they did the circle after the match together, they have the reward together in front of the fans.

These are the moments and I think they’re well aware of what they did, they know what it took today and they’re just fully committed, they’re a team that’s fully committed and full of belief.

News.title: Defending champion Sinner overcomes slow start to reach third round
News.content:
The very best of Jannik Sinner is yet to be glimpsed at Wimbledon 2026. Yet, even if the version seen so far on Centre Court hasn’t quite matched the sheer relentlessness that characterises Sinner at his best, the world No 1 still sealed a straight-sets victory to advance to the third round.

For the bulk of the first two sets, Nuno Borges played terrific tennis, with his aggressive groundstrokes underpinned by powerful serving. Borges held his first ten service games; after losing the first set in a tie-break, he had an opportunity to serve out the second set.

Sinner might even have had flashbacks to the last time that he played a Grand Slam second-round match: his defeat in the French Open this year.

At 5-4 and 40-30 up, Borges was a point away from levelling the match. Instead, he slammed his backhand down the line into the top of the net. Sinner then benefited from a fortuitous net cord, tilting the point in his favour before lobbing Borges.

With a forehand into the net, Borges lost the break point, then looked to the sky, despairing at a chance that he sensed would not come again. Such is the brutality of playing Sinner.

News.title: South East house prices suffer weakest growth in Britain
News.content:
House prices in the South East are rising at the slowest pace in Britain amid warnings Andy Burnham risks creating a North-South divide in the property market.

Property values in the region, excluding London, rose by just 0.1pc in the second quarter of the year, according to the Nationwide house price index.

By contrast, the rate of growth in the North and North West of England was 3.9pc.

It has raised concerns that Andy Burnham could “turbocharge” a North-South divide in house price growth under his plans to boost regional economic activity.

The man expected to be Britain’s next prime minister could create a bounce in Northern house prices, according to Garrington Property Finders, the UK’s largest property buying agency.

Jonathan Hopper, chief executive of the company which researches and sources properties for investors, said: “The North-South divide continues to grow and could be turbocharged by a Prime Minister Burnham.

“A huge injection of government spending into the North could create a Burnham bounce that accelerates northern price growth further.”

Mr Burnham set out his political aspirations in a speech in Manchester this week, pledging to create “growth in every postcode”.

Prices in the South East remained higher than all other areas of Britain apart from London, with the average home worth £341,175. In London, house prices rose 1.6pc to £540,903 in the second quarter.

House prices in Northern Ireland rose at the fastest pace in the UK at 8.6pc – nearly quadruple the national pace over the last year. The average home there was worth £226,699.

Nationally, property values were up 2.2pc to £278,784 in June compared with the same month last year.

However, prices flatlined between May and June after the Iran war pushed up mortgage rates.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said: “It is not surprising that the market has softened a little in recent months, given the uncertainty caused by developments in the Middle East and the subsequent rise in energy prices and market interest rates.

“Indeed, consumer confidence and measures of housing sentiment have weakened, and mortgage approvals fell noticeably in May.”

Ashley Webb, an economist at Capital Economics, said: “The stagnation in the Nationwide measure of house prices in June shows that the rise in mortgage rates triggered by the Iran war continues to weigh on the housing market.”

Sports.title: Portugal vs Croatia facing weather delay as storm threatens to wreck Ronaldo and Modric’s World Cup clash
Sports.content:
THE last 32 clash between Portugal and Croatia could face delays after reports of a storm in the area.

The European heavyweights will battle in Toronto, Canada this evening (Thursday) where Cristiano Ronaldo will dance against his former Real Madrid team-mate Luka Modric, both playing in what will surely be their final major tournament.



Extreme weather is expected around the time of the game at the Toronto Stadium.



Temperatures will reach 32°C with a heat index of 42°C, and there is a risk of thunderstorms during the match.

FIFA has introduced cooling measures, but lightning within 13 km of the stadium would cause delays.

Portugal’s training was nearly cancelled yesterday due to strong winds in the area.

Mexico’s last 32 clash with Ecuador was delayed due to thunderstorms and England’s last friendly before the World Cup against Costa Rica was delayed by over an hour for the same reason following torrential rain.

Sports.title: ‘The time has come’ – Former Man Utd boss QUITS huge role at European giant
Sports.content:
LOUIS VAN GAAL says he has made the shock decision to quit Ajax after seeing his closest allies leave.

The former Manchester United boss, 74, worked as an adviser to the supervisory board since October 2023.





But Van Gaal has resigned as preparations are made for the new Eredivisie season.

And the managerial legend revealed he knew it was time to walk away after the departures of Micheal van Praag, Alex Kroes and Marijn Beuker from their roles.

Van Gaal said: ”Michael van Praag is a friend of mine, and we worked well together at Ajax in the past.

“As chairman of the supervisory board at the time, he approached me in 2023, and I was happy to help both him and Ajax.



“There were a lot of changes in key positions, and there was too little football expertise at that time.

“As an external adviser, I was then able to play a role in filling important football positions, such as the appointments of Alex Kroes and Marijn Beuker.

“During that period, more football knowledge was also brought into the organisation.

“But Michael stepped down in 2025, Alex left, and Marijn has now also departed. For me, the time has now come to step down as well.”

Van Gaal took the job after already writing his name into the Ajax history books as one of their most successful managers.

During a six-year spell in charge, between 1991 and 1997, he lifted silverware 11 TIMES.

His trophy haul included three Eredivisie titles and one Champions League crown.

Van Gaal has gone on to have three spells in charge of the Netherlands, along with managing the likes of Barcelona and Bayern Munich.



The Dutchman won the FA Cup during his two-year stint in the Old Trafford dugout.

But Van Gaal was brutally sacked just 48 hours after beating Manchester City at Wembley.

Sports.title: All the pubs that will DEFINITELY open for England’s 1am World Cup clash in huge boost for fans
Sports.content:
IN a huge boost for England fans, ALL pubs are set to be allowed to stay open until 5am for the Three Lions’ World Cup last-16 clash against Mexico on Monday.

Pubs had previously been told they needed a temporary licence to screen the high-stakes game.





But after an outcry from fans and politicians, Sir Keir Starmer is expected to lay an emergency law in Parliament so supporters can pack out boozers across the country.

It’s not clear how many venues will take up the option to stay open for the 1am game in Mexico, which may not finish until 3.30am if it goes to extra time and penalties.

With just three days to go before kick-off, it’s likely that not all pubs will be prepared to host a Monday night party.

But The Sun has compiled a list of all the pubs around the country that are ALREADY certain to be open for the clash.



London

A number of late-night venues across the capital will take advantage of their long opening hours to screen the football.

Fans will hope that the now famous viral scenes from the Euros of ecstatic supporters at Boxpark can be recreated as its Wembley, Shoreditch and Croydon will be staying open until the end of the game.

Club venues like the Clapham Grand, Village Underground in Shoreditch and the Steel Yard in Hackney will be converted into fan zones to cheer on Thomas Tuchel’s side.

Those looking for a more traditional pub atmosphere can head to the Kings Head in Crouch End, which will be showing the game.



Manchester

Supporters in Manchester are being treated to some of the country’s biggest fan zones this weekend, with a festival-like atmosphere expected.

Massive city-centre venue Freight Island is hosting a huge fan zone, with giant screens, food stalls and thousands of supporters expected to attend the late night kick-off.

Iconic music venue New Century Hall, which has hosted everyone from Jimi Hendrix to Tina Turner will now host England fans cheering on the Three Lions as the space is transformed into a fan zone.

A lively atmosphere is also expected at the Grosvenor, which is showing the game.



Liverpool

Liverpool’s famous warehouse venue, Camp and Furnace, is hosting an all-night England party, with doors opening from 8pm and a free drink thrown in with tickets.

Those looking for a pub atmosphere can turn to Punch Tarmey’s; the giant Irish bar on the docks will be packed with supporters for the 1am kick-off and promises one of the loudest atmospheres in town.

And as in London the city’s Boxpork will also be showing the fixture.

How can I find out if my local boozer is screening the game? A number of other pubs are also expected to show the game; announcements will come in the coming days. To ensure your local boozer is screening the match, your first port of call should be their social media pages. Most pubs will loudly advertise if they’ll be open late for the 1am kickoff. You can also use online sports pub finders like FANZO, which update in real-time to show which venues are open for late-night World Cup action.

Newcastle

Geordies will be looking to cheer on their hometown hero, Elliot Anderson, in the round of 16 clash, and a number of venues are open across the city.

Trendy outdoor venue Ouseburn Garden, which boasts an impressive big screen, will be showing the match.



Stack, another beer garden option in the city, also hosts a number of street food vendors.

Bristol

Legendary music venue the Fleece, is swapping gigs for goals, with four giant screens and free entry for England supporters.

If fans are searching for a pub atmosphere, the Cat and Wheel, with its impressive beer garden will be showing the game in the early hours.

Birmingham

In Birmingham Luna Springs, a huge outdoor venue, is hosting one of the city’s biggest World Cup parties, staying open until 3am for the Mexico showdown.



Sports bar Box, which has venues in Leeds, London and Manchester as well as Birmingham will be showing the clash across its multiple screens.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nottingham

Iconic Nottingham club NG-One will be transformed into the City’s biggest dedicated football event, with DJs, giant screens and hundreds of supporters expected to attend.

Also promising a festival-like atmosphere on Sunday night is Nottingham’s Secret Garden, which will boast eight screens in total as well as food, DJs, and entertainment.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid ‘make transfer enquiry for Mason Greenwood with ex-Man Utd forward lined up to replace Julian Alvarez’
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester United winger Mason Greenwood is reportedly set to be offered a big-money move to Atletico Madrid.

The LaLiga giants are preparing to splash the cash after talisman Julian Alvarez publicly confirmed he wants to quit.





Atletico have rejected bids worth up to £130million from rivals Real Madrid and Barcelona as they desperately attempt to change the Argentine’s mind.

But they have been scouring the market for potential replacements in case Alvarez keeps pushing for a move.

And L’Equipe report Atletico have made an enquiry to sign Greenwood, 24, from Marseille.

He bagged 26 goals and notched 11 assists in 45 appearances for the French giants last season.

That form has resulted in Marseille demanding £43m as they look to raise funds after missing out on Champions League qualification.

But Atletico have not been put off by the lofty price tag and there are suggestions they will lodge a formal bid soon.

Man Utd still own 40 per cent of Greenwood’s economic rights – leading to the Spanish side also reaching out to Old Trafford chiefs over a deal.

The one-cap England man left the Red Devils in a £27m deal and has gone on to rediscover his best form with Marseille.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Greenwood has found the net 48 times since heading to the south coast of France.

And Atletico’s interest has come after it was initially claimed he had agreed personal terms with Turkish side Fenerbahce.

Presidential candidate Hakan Safi promised to land Greenwood before being beaten in the race by Aziz Yildirim.

Roma and Saudi Arabian big-spenders Al-Hilal have also been linked with a summer swoop.



Greenwood was frozen out of the Man Utd squad in January 2022, after facing charges of attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour.

They were later dropped but he was sent out on loan to Getafe before making a permanent move to Marseille in July 2024.

Sports.title: Germany ‘tell Julian Nagelsmann resign or be SACKED’ after humiliating World Cup exit with Klopp tipped to replace him
Sports.content:
GERMANY boss Julian Nagelsmann has reportedly been urged to resign by the country’s FA after their disastrous World Cup campaign.

Nagelsmann’s side were dumped out in the Round of 32 by Paraguay on penalties in one of the biggest shocks in the tournament’s history.





And the DFB, football’s governing body in Germany, have told the ex-Bayern Munich boss he must resign or he’ll be axed.

Sky in Germany say a decision over Nagelsmann’s position is “expected soon” after the 38-year-old was asked to explain Germany’s poor tournament in the US.

Former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp an early favourite to replace him.

German media slammed the team’s performance against Paraguay, with the game ending 1-1 after extra time.



Kai Havertz equalised in the second half after ex-Brighton star Julio Enciso opened the scoring – before Paraguay triumphed 4-3 on spot kicks.

It was the first time Germany had ever lost a penalty shootout.

German newspaper Bild dubbed it “a night of shame” and the DFB cancelled a scheduled press conference for Nagelsmann on Tuesday.

But Nagelsmann insisted he would not walk away from the role despite rising pressure on his position.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “I am not someone who runs away. This is not the first time this has happened, and there are some things about today that need to be changed.

“But if the DFB wants me to continue I am going to continue. I know the mechanics of football, I know how the industry works.

“I know a lot of people will want me to leave but I would love to continue if the football association wants me to.“

But former Liverpool and Germany midfielder Dietmar Hamann tore into Nagelsmann’s lack of commitment to the demands of the job.



He told RTE: “This is a guy who rarely watches games, rarely watches games.

“He’s never been once in Milan to watch [Yann] Bisseck play. He should’ve gone to the World Cup.

“He’s never been to Brentford in two-and-a-half years to watch [Kevin] Schade… In the Bundesliga, he might be watching one or two games a month.

“There’s Champions League games where Real Madrid played (against Bayern). We had the Africa Cup of Nations in January, where he could have watched (group stage opponents) Ivory Coast and some of the potential opponents. He didn’t go.

“The Club World Cup last season, where you play these venues, the weather conditions, the heat.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“(Portugal coach Roberto) Martinez is here, Tuchel is here. [France coach Didier] Deschamps, who’s won everything, is in his mid-60s, is in America for three weeks.

“Who’s not there? Our man. This is where I’ve got no sympathy for him.”

Sports.title: Will pubs be open for England vs Mexico? Late license laws for the World Cup clash explained
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fever has officially gripped the nation after Harry Kane’s dramatic late goals against DR Congo fired the Three Lions into the World Cup Round of 16.

Thomas Tuchel’s men are marching on to face Mexico this Monday (June 6), but millions of bleary-eyed fans have been left facing a total nightmare.





The high-stakes clash kicks off at 1am UK time on Monday morning.

Supporters are begging Prime Minister Keir Starmer to grant a snap Bank Holiday Monday so the nation can recover from what promises to be an epic and potentially booze-fuelled night of tension.

Fans have pointed out that Scotland got a long weekend, so why shouldn’t England fans get a proper lie-in to back the boys?

Sadly, Downing Street has given a firm “no” to a day off, meaning millions face a Monday morning hangover from hell at their desks.



What are the license laws for England’s World Cup 2026 games?

Earlier this summer, the Government threw football fans a lifeline.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood brought in The Licensing Act 2003 (FIFA World Cup Licensing Hours) Order 2026.

The nationwide rule allows boozers across England and Wales to extend their opening hours automatically for major knockout matches.



Usually, pub landlords have to wade through red tape and pay heavy fees to keep the pints flowing past their standard closing times.

But under these special World Cup laws, if England is playing a knockout match that kicks off between 5pm and 9pm, pubs can legally stay open until 1am.

Even better, for later games starting between 9pm and 10pm, last orders are pushed back to 2am.

The Home Office called it an “open goal” to help the hospitality industry and let fans celebrate together without getting ushered out mid-penalty shootout.

Will those license rules apply for the Mexico game on Monday?

Unfortunately, because Mexico is co-hosting the tournament, the local 6pm kickoff in Mexico City means a 1am start time here in Britain.



The emergency government licensing extension only applies to matches that kick off on or before 10pm UK time.

Because the Three Lions are playing in the dead of night, the blanket rule is completely useless for Monday morning’s big game.

Punters hoping to stroll into their regular local at midnight could find the doors locked and the lights off.

Will pubs be able to open at 1am Monday morning?

But don’t panic just yet, it isn’t completely game over.

While there’s no automatic nationwide extension, individual pubs can still open to show the match and serve alcohol in the early hours.



But pub owners will have had to apply for a Temporary Event Notice (TEN) from their local council weeks in advance.

Usually, TEN’s must be submitted to the local council at least 10 working days before the event takes place – many pubs may have missed this deadline.

But Sir Keir Starmer is poised to let all pubs stay open until 5am for the World Cup clash, The Sun understands.

Sir Keir is said to be exploring options to extend that universal lifting of restrictions for a one-off.

The outgoing PM is expected to lay an emergency law in Parliament so fans can watch the Three Lions take on Mexico in the boozer.



Organised, football-focused landlords will have already secured the required notices to make sure fans can watch Jude Bellingham and the team (hopefully) do us proud.

But it’s entirely up to each pub boss whether they want to pay the staff and open up at 1am on a Monday morning.

How to check if your local pub is open

Nobody wants to wander the streets looking for a pint at midnight.

To ensure your local boozer is screening the match, your first port of call should be their social media pages.

Most pubs will loudly advertise if they’ve bagged a special late-night license for the 1am kickoff.



You can also use online sports pub finders like FANZO, which update in real-time to show which venues are open for late-night World Cup action.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you’re still unsure, pop into your local over the weekend and ask the landlord directly.

If the option is there, make sure to book a table, because spaces will disappear fast.

Sports.title: Brilliant moment England fans take over baseball game and fall for MLB star – as crowd beg them to come back every week
Sports.content:
ENGLAND fans took over the Atlanta Braves baseball match last night, with MLB fans begging them to come back every week.

After beating DR Congo in a 12pm kick-off in Atlanta fans flocked to Truist Park, home of the Braves, to get some drinks in and soak up one of America’s biggest sports.





That, though, came as quite a shock to the usual crowd at Truist Park, and one player in particular.

After settling into one stand for the 7:15 pm match, fans began an affliction with Michael Harris II.

Usually his nickname is ‘Money Mike’.

Last night, he became ‘Money Michael’.



When in the field, he was the closest player to the England supporters, and he played up to the crowd who consistently sang songs about him and cheered his every move.

Chants directed at Harris were typically British, and you can listen to them in the video in this article.

They included, “Harris give us a wave. Harris, Harris, give us a wave.”

“Baseball‘s coming home again, with Michael Harris!”, “There’s only one Michael Harris”, and “Walking in a Harris wonderland”.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Braves regulars were coming over to the England fans, taking selfies with them, offering to buy them drinks, and begging for them to come back every week.

That may be down to the fact that the Braves are in a patch of bad form, but were cheered on to a win by the Brits.

The Braves’ DJ clearly knew how to play up to the crowd too.

At full-time, it was almost exclusively Oasis playing through the speakers, with a host of England supporters belting out Wonderwall before heading to the front row to chant for Harris himself to come over.

Harris himself clearly appreciated the support.



After winning the game, he did eventually come over to the travelling England support and took selfies and signed shirts, while drinking in the atmosphere and posting a video to his Instagram story of his new-found fan club.

He was even gifted an England shirt by SunSport’s Lloyd Canfield, which he took home with him – Harris was kind enough to offer him his match-worn baseball cap in exchange.

SunSport’s footage of the England fans went viral on social media, with the Atlanta Braves, Michael Harris and MLB all sharing the love online.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And while England fans got a new favourite baseball player, American fans fell in love with English football fans that little bit more.

Sports.title: Boost for England fans as ALL pubs set to be allowed to open for 1am World Cup clash with Mexico
Sports.content:
SIR Keir Starmer is poised to let all pubs stay open until 5am for England’s World Cup clash on Monday, The Sun understands.

The outgoing PM is expected to lay an emergency law in Parliament so fans can watch the Three Lions take on Mexico in the boozer.





The 1am kick-off time means that currently pubs have to have a special permit to open through the night, and the deadline to acquire one has already passed.

It has sparked calls for blanket licensing laws to be relaxed further so the nation can cheer on Harry Kane and the boys in their local.

The Home Office has already given pubs permission to open late during England’s World Cup knockout matches.

But Monday’s round-of-16 match at the Azteca falls outside that window because of its 1am kick-off time.



Footie-mad Sir Keir has spent the afternoon exploring options to extend that universal lifting of restrictions for a one-off.

He is expected to lay a statutory instrument in the Common tomorrow relaxing licensing laws further.

While the final details will be announced, it is understood pubs will be able to serve until around 5am to allow for possible extra time and penalties.

The deadline to apply for a Temporary Event Notice passed earlier this week before it was guaranteed that England would make the last 16.



Earlier today a business minister sparked anger after confirming that pubs without one would not be able to open their bars up to fans.

Reform’s Robert Jenrick blasted: “This is ridiculous. Just issue a decree that any pub in the land can stay open late on Monday.

“It’s been done before. Stop being pettifogging killjoys and get behind England.”

Lib Dem Home Affairs spokesman Max Wilkinson has said: “Pubs face missing out on a much needed opportunity to get more money into the till and England fans will be missing out on the opportunity to watch their team together in their local with a beer for the biggest game of the tournament so far.

“The Government must back our hospitality venues and allow England fans to cheer on the Three Lions as they head to Mexico.”



Meanwhile some killjoy councils have even been denying pubs’ requests for a Temporary Event Notice because of noise fears.

It saw Community Secretary Steve Reed order them to stop being spoilsports and be more lenient than usual.

He said: “If pubs want to open their doors for World Cup matches they should be able to.

“We’ve relaxed licensing rules to make this possible, but it seems that some councils are still saying no.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is my message to them – if you can say yes, do it and this government will back you.



“There’s nothing like watching the World Cup in your local – let’s make it happen.”

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: USA red card drama, Rice injury latest after England scare, Senegal fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon inspired by 'phenomenal' Harry Kane

Anthony Gordon says Harry Kane is an "inspiration to all of us" after saved England's World Cup hopes with two goals against the DR Congo.

Thomas Tuchel's men were heading for faliure when they trailed 1-0 with less than 15 minutes remaining in the match. But winger Gordon climbed off the bench to twice set up Kane, who first headed home and then thrashed an unstoppable drive into the top corner.

After the match, Gordon said: "You know what? As soon as he hit (the second goal), I knew it was going in. I was already celebrating.

"It's more the consistency that he surprised me with. Anyone can score a good goal, anyone at this level can put the ball in the top corner. This is the consistency that he does it. Every day in training. Every game. He is phenomenal. He plays at such a high, high level.

"It's amazing to be around him every day, because when you're around someone at the elite level – he's at the very, very top of football, he's having a season that’s only ever been beaten by Lionel Messi, the greatest footballer of all time. So that speaks to the level he's playing at.

"When you're around someone like that, you want to pick up as many habits and watch everything he does to see why he's at that level. It’s no accident, like I said, there’s consistency every day, how hard he works, every finishing drill.

"He does it with passion, he does it with seriousness. He never ever messes about. So it's amazing to be around him. He’s definitely an inspiration to all of us."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi in stitches as airport security stop Argentina star and confiscate item
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi in stitches as airport security stop Argentina star and confiscate item

The Argentina captain showed a different side to his usual composed self as he burst out in hysterics while navigating airport security

View 3 Images Lionel Messi laughed uncontrollably as his Argentina team-mates were examined by airport staff (Image: X/Eldesmarque)

Many have theorised that Lionel Messi is from another planet due to his incredible goalscoring exploits, but more evidence has been uncovered to prove that he is, in fact, just as human as the rest of us. First, he missed a penalty at the World Cup 2026 against Austria and now, the Argentina superstar is also showing a side to him that's rarely seen before.

‌



The 39-year-old was due to fly back to his home in Miami on Thursday with the team as they fly down for their round of 32 clash with Cabo Verde on Friday evening. As many nations have experienced before flying on their private charter planes, footballers are not immune to Transportation Security Administration (TSA) checks from airport security staff on the tarmac.

‌



In video footage captured by Eldesmarque, Messi can be seen lining up with his Albiceleste team-mates such as Rodrigo De Paul and Cristian Romero as they prepared to board their plane. Minutes later, the Argentina skipper can be seen sporting a huge grin on his face.

‌



One particular moment had Messi in fits of laughter after airport security examined the suitcase belonging to Tottenham captain Romero. The players, just like any passengers, were forced to put their luggage through the scanners and walk through metal detectors.

Cape Verde have support of Shamrock Rovers as they change plans to watch Lionel Messi clash READ MORE :

Lionel Messi has caused Argentina a huge problem as his country’s media set him task READ MORE :

Unfortunately, not everyone made it through without a hitch. The footage appeared to show one security staff member pull a large object out of Romero's luggage, which was reported to be a huge spark lighter.

Messi was alert to the issue and when he saw the sheer size of it, the Inter Miami star couldn't contain his laughter as he chuckled away in front of his fellow Argentina colleagues. Security didn't seem to see the funny side of it as the item appeared to be confiscated.

‌



View 3 Images Cristian Romero's item appears to be confiscated by security (Image: X/Eldesmarque)

View 3 Images Lionel Messi also has his baggage checked by security (Image: X/Eldesmarque)

‌



Footage captured from the scene spread on social media as Messi's rarely-seen comical side was put on display for the world to see. It's clear the Rosario-born icon is savouring the last weeks of what many expect will be his sixth and final tournament.

It's been a superb World Cup for Messi so far, having bagged a hat-trick against Algeria in addition to a brace against Austria and his solitary strike against Jordan. He tops the goalscoring charts with six goals in three games so far and many would expect the former Barcelona star to get on the scoresheet against Cabo Verde again.

‌



The Argentinian magician has already broken the all-time World Cup goalscoring record at the tournament, with France's Kylian Mbappe in the hot pursuit. With 19 goals already to his name, Messi will be eager to stretch the gap in their upcoming knockout game.

Lionel Scaloni's side have looked well-equipped to defend their title as world champions after breezing through the group stage with three wins from as many games. Argentina face Cabo Verde on Friday, July 3, with an 11pm kick-off at Miami Stadium.

Sports.title: Cape Verde have support of Shamrock Rovers as they change plans to watch Lionel Messi clash
Sports.content:
Cape Verde have support of Shamrock Rovers as they change plans to watch Lionel Messi clash

Cape Verde have Pico Lopes in their ranks as they eye an almighty World Cup shock against Argentina and Lionel Messi - but they'll have the backing of Shamrock Rovers

View 2 Images Cape Verde's Pico Lopes plays his club football for Shamrock Rovers

Shamrock Rovers have a vital stop to make en-route home to Dublin following their crunch league game at Sligo Rovers. To watch their captain go head-to-head with the greatest footballer of all time.

‌



Under normal circumstances, Pico Lopes would have been leading Rovers at Sligo's The Showgrounds (capacity 3,873), in a bid to help them extend their lead at the top of the League of Ireland Premier Division.

‌



Instead, he will be facing off with Lionel Messi and Argentina in the World Cup knockout stages. In front of 65,000 fans in the Miami Stadium, on behalf of Cape Verde. And his team-mates have no intention of missing it.

‌



So when Rovers' game at Sligo has finished, the team will turn their attentions to where to see the greatest moment in their club's history. The match will not be available to watch back at Rovers' Tallaght Stadium. It is owned by the council and there is no facility to show it.

Cristiano Ronaldo faces World Cup knockout hoodoo as Portugal drought hangs over him READ MORE :

Rovers press officer Mark Lynch said: "Our game will finish about an hour before Pico's match kicks off. So the team want to find a pub somewhere on the way back that is showing it. The team bus will be stopping. We're taking about 400-500 fans as well. I don't know what their plans are. They will be looking to stream it on various platforms."

Rovers have a crucial Champions League first-leg qualifier at Maltese champions Floriana on Tuesday, which Lopes had hoped to be involved in, should he fail to become part of the biggest shock in World Cup history.

‌



But Lynch insists the circumstances involved in Lopes getting back in time to be available, mean he won't be. He would target the return leg in Ireland instead a week later. But when Lopes does return to the club, Lynch insists the defender will be treated just the same.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi will have to down the African side if he wants a second World Cup (Image: 2026 Eurasia Sport Images)

Irrespective of the fact he is now 'probably the most famous footballer in Ireland.' Lynch said: "Within the group he will be treated just the same. And he would want that. He's a humble fella. One of the good guys.

‌



"The vibe has been great. The media interest in him has ignited. Everything has been amplified. And if Cape Verde beat Argentina, they will have basically won the World Cup. He's probably the most famous footballer in Ireland, but all the publicity won't change him."

And what chances Lopes could end up with a priceless memento - Messi's shirt. "Well, he'll have hold of it for the full 90 minutes, so he might as well get it from him (Messi) at the final whistle," added Lynch.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo faces World Cup knockout hoodoo as Portugal drought hangs over him
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo faces World Cup knockout hoodoo as Portugal drought hangs over him

Cristiano Ronaldo will have to revisit his knockout nightmare when Portugal face Croatia - and he's doing so whilst struggling for form and having his role questioned

View 3 Images Cristiano Ronaldo is still looking to score a knockout goal at his sixth World Cup (Image: Edmund Wong/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

On the relatively small list of Cristiano Ronaldo 'have nots' winning a World Cup is one them - but before that scoring in a knockout game might be a good place to start.

‌



The Portuguese sensation in playing at his sixth World Cup - a joint record. He's played in 25 games - four off the record. That is a nod to his longevity, but it makes his dire record in the knockout stages all the more jarring.

‌



Ronaldo's - and as a result Portugal's - World Cup has been dominated by talk of whether Father Time has well and truly caught him up. Below par showings in games with DR Congo and Colombia, where Portugal scored once across the 180 minutes, were attributed to the lack of team fluency - for which Ronaldo was held responsible.

‌



His brace against Uzbekistan, playing at their first World Cup and ranked 60th in the world, was as meek a 'response' you could possibly get. His chorus of fans, led by Piers Morgan, cited his killer instinct, but we're yet to see that when it really counts.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum sends message to son after proving World Cup doubters wrong READ MORE :

Cristiano Ronaldo consoles Chelsea legend after father's death as World Cup exit confirmed READ MORE :

Ronaldo's World Cup record doesn't make for overly present reading as it is. And his lack of knockout goals are perhaps a reflection of that. His 2006 exploits, where he helped Portugal make the last four, came before he morphed into the world-leading player he became. The team's success was very much due to the collective, not one superstar.

Since then the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has seen his last three World Cups end in the group stage (2014), the last 16 (losing to Uruguay) and the quarter-finals (losing to Morocco).

‌



Ronaldo scored a hat-trick in a group stage draw against Spain in 2018 and also scored against Morocco in that same tournament - giving him a total of four goals - his best at a World Cup. For context, Harry Kane's best is six, Kylian Mbappe's is eight and Lionel Messi's is seven.

Ronaldo's six other goals have come in group matches against Iran, North Korea, Ghana (two) and the brace he recently hit against Uzbekistan.

View 3 Images Cristiano Ronaldo's hat-trick vs Spain in 2018 in his most impressive exploit in front of goal at a World Cup (Image: (Photo credit should read NELSON ALMEIDA/AFP via Getty Images))

‌



That is not the record of a man who has forged a reputation as one of the game's elite goal scorers. More of one who takes his moments against the lesser sides but can't back it up come crunch time.

That is of course not Ronaldo's modus operandi throughout his career, but there's no denying that his great exploits have come at club level. Unlike great rival Messi, who can boast an outstanding legacy on the international stage as well as the club one.

Croatia present Ronaldo with the next chance to get the knockout monkey off his back. The 2018 finalists finished second to England in their group, but have shown themselves to be a wise tournament team. Ronaldo has twice found the net against the Croatians - the most recent of those coming two years ago in the Nations League.

‌



There has been little to no appetite to mix up the Portugal forward line, with Ronaldo firmly the one Roberto Martinez will turn to. He recently claimed that overlooking or hauling off the greatest scorer in football history would be a bonkers move.

View 3 Images Plenty watching on believe the Portugal icon is not justifying his starting role (Image: Charlotte Wilson, Getty Images)

Maybe so if this was Ronaldo in his pomp, but the modern-day version is not the same beast. After keeping him scoreless, DR Congo midfielder Ngal’ayel Mukau claimed they had no special plan to deal with the 41-year-old, adding: "We know he isn’t the same as before. He’s a bit older now."

‌



Martinez used 22 members of his squad in the World Cup group stage, rotating everybody apart from one. Ronaldo played every minute. Common sense suggests making your oldest player your most used player, isn't the wisest move.

Go back four years ago and former Portugal boss Fernando Santos showed the courage to bench Ronaldo for the last-16 clash against Switzerland. Portugal won 6-1 - their biggest World Cup margin of victory since 2010.

Few men seem to seek the individual limelight like the Real Madrid great. Conversely, great rival Messi and former team-mate Luka Modric are content to go about their business. Modric has become the oldest player ever to record an assist at a World Cup. Messi's efforts are well publicised, all casting a shadow over Ronaldo.

Sports.title: Couple's chilling warning to England fans travelling to Mexico for World Cup after 'terrifying experience'
Sports.content:
Couple's chilling warning to England fans travelling to Mexico for World Cup after 'terrifying experience'

EXCLUSIVE: Warning to England fans travelling to Mexico for the World Cup Round of 16 clash, after a British couple's 'terrifying experience' earlier in tournament

England fans warn of dangers of Mexico fan zones

Two England fans, who have already been to the World Cup in Mexico City, described their “terrifying experience”.

‌



Jo Lewis and partner Gary Taylor said it was a horrendous few hours in and around an official FanFest. They warned Three Lions supporters heading to England’s round of 16 game to be very careful.

‌



Jo feared for her life. And Gary, who has attended hundreds of Spurs and England matches said: “Mexico City was the worst - 100 percent the worst experience of all the matches I’ve ever been.”

‌



They were speaking after it was revealed three Mexicans were suffocated and died during wild celebrations after their win over Ecuador. More than one million fans took to the streets of the capital following the historic win, leading to severe crushing. Jo and Gary visited Mexico City for the opening game last month - before heading to Dallas to support England.

View 4 Images Fans hit the streets of Mexico City - three people died (Image: Getty Images)

Councils urged to let pubs to stay open later for England's 1am World Cup clash READ MORE :

England sets sights on Mexico as Three Lions labour against Leopards READ MORE :

They described chaotic scenes in the Fanfest. The couple, from Harold Wood, Essex said they wanted all England fans travelling down to Mexico for Sunday’s game to be aware of the issues.

‌



They said policing, security and organisation were severely lacking compared with the United States.

View 4 Images Warning about Mexico fans in World Cup (Image: Cristian Leyva/Jna Press/Nexpher via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Jo, 44, who works in logistics for an oil and gas company, said: “People with children, with babies were all getting crushed. It was terrible. No-one cared. People getting crushed everywhere.

‌



“It took us four hours to get into the fanzone. I was swept in on a surge of grown adults into a small doorway area - my feet weren’t even on the floor - and I couldn’t see Gary, and I started to panic.

View 4 Images Warning about Mexico fans in World Cup (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

“We weren’t together and that was petrifying for me. This was the worst experience of my life. My hands were trembling for at least an hour afterwards.”

‌



Gary, 64, an estate agent, said: “We went together to Mexico to see the Azteca stadium and to experience the Mexican fans. We arrived in the main square, and there was so many people. It was chaotic.

View 4 Images Superfams Gary Taylor and Jo Lewis warn Enfgland fans of dangers in Mexico (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

“There must have been a two or three mile queue just to get to the fanzone. There was just one entrance which was, perhaps, the size of two double garage doors.

‌



“It was frightening. Literally 10,000 people squeezing though that gap. It was madness absolute madness.”

Gary and Jo are going to every England game and have tickets for the final if England make it to the match in New York on July 19.

They will be joined in Mexico by an estimated 5,000 Three Lions supporters for a match that will be played in a frenzied passionate atmosphere. It kicks off at 1am on Monday morning UK time - 6pm local time.

Article continues below

England will fly in two days before the match. Mexico fans kept previous opponents Ecuador awake by letting off fireworks outside their hotel.

Sports.title: McInnes Q&A on transfer targets, new signings, Ferguson interest & more!
Sports.content:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes says the club are working on making more summer signings after adding five players in the opening weeks of the transfer window.

The Ibrox club have added goalkeeper Ivan Pandur, former player Ross McCrorie, Scotland striker Lawrence Shankland, Dan Neil after his Sunderland contract expired, plus defender Ben Godfrey on loan from Atalanta.

McInnes says he wants "ready-made" players to help "meet demands" this season but admitted the club may need to be "patient at times" as they navigate the transfer window.

Following Jack Butland's £3m move to Hull City, McInnes revealed others will depart Ibrox as he shapes his squad ahead of their Scottish Premiership opener at Dundee Utd on July 31, live on Sky Sports.

The former Hearts, Kilmarnock, Aberdeen, Bristol City and St Johnstone boss also addressed interest in Bologna and Scotland star Lewis Ferguson, plus the future of in-demand midfielder Nicolas Raskin who has impressed with Belgium at the World Cup.

Here is McInnes' full interview with Sky Sports News...

How have the first couple of weeks gone as Rangers manager?

Yes, good. Obviously, the first week, [there were] a lot of conversations about trying to see how the squad would shape up. The last week's been great, just getting back into things and obviously getting that introduction to the players here, integrating the new signings.

Image: Derek McInnes left Hearts to take up the Rangers job last month

Obviously, there's been a lot of good work done by the club, and it's well documented we're trying to bring a few more in before the start of the season, if we can.

The pre-season has gone well. It's there to get the players fit for the full campaign, not just for the first game. The players have been working extremely hard. I feel that pre-season is a necessary evil for players; they've got to understand that. It's got to be that single-mindedness to work through it and be as fit and as strong as you possibly can. The application has been first class, and I'm really enjoying just getting to know everybody in and around the club.

Image: Ben Godfrey is on loan at Rangers from Atalanta

Pleased with the business done already?

Yes, there is good work being done. A lot of these conversations were ongoing ahead of my appointment, but obviously, in meetings with the recruitment team, Jim [Gillespie] and Andrew [Cavenagh], we were clear in what we're looking for in terms of key positions, and the types of players we want to bring to the club as well.

I think what we have had with the signings is a mixture of all that, but 'good types' underpins everything. There are a few players familiar to Scottish football, something we want in the squad, and room for players who are coming to Scotland and Rangers for the first time.

Image: Scotland striker Lawrence Shankland was Rangers' first summer signing from Hearts

We as a club can give players so much with success and the reward and everything else it comes with. It's a brilliant club to play for if you're winning. So, we've got a lot that we can sell, but equally, we need players to know what they can bring us.

What we need at this moment in time is ready-made, good types of players in the building, players who train right every day, players who have the right approach, that winning mentality, and that leadership quality that every manager looks for in their team.

Image: Former Sunderland captain Dan Neil turned down Southampton to join Rangers

Are there other areas you would still like to strengthen?

Yes, there are areas. I'm not going into specifics now, but there are clearly a lot of conversations going on. We've got a lot of players in the building at the minute, and I'm looking forward to getting to know the players that are already here. From the outside looking in, you can have a set opinion, but it's only really working with players day in, day out that you can really forge that opinion better.

There are some players here that are catching the eye already and doing well in training. But there will be a natural progression; there will be players moving out the way to get players in. Streamlining the squad and getting the right number is very important as well - but, as I say, we're a long way from that. We're a long way from the end of the window closing.

Image: McInnes has inherited a large squad at Rangers

We want to be as strong as we can for the first game against Dundee United. So, there's a lot of work to do, both physically, integration of players, getting the players up to match speed, and also a lot of work to do to try and bring players in as quickly as possible. Sometimes you need to wait for the better ones, and we need to just be patient at times, as well as still being forthright in our intentions.

What is the process to appoint a new captain?

Image: Former captain James Tavernier left Rangers after 11 years in the summer

James [Tavernier] has moved on now and he's been the captain here for a long time. It is always something that people get obsessed about, and always will ask you about, but I'm actually quite relaxed about it at the minute.

Obviously, somebody's got to take the team down the tunnel, and somebody's got to be the club captain, and it is a big honour for him to be captain of the club, but I'm trying to fill the dressing room with a lot of captains. Then, I'll have the benefit and the luxury of being able to choose one. At the minute we're a long way from making that decision. I'd like to think we're going to get a number of good, viable options who can take that role on.

Confident chairman Andrew Cavenagh and the board will back you to make a marquee signing?

Image: Rangers chairman Andrew Cavenagh has backed Derek McInnes to succeed at the club

Yes, I think there have been discussions had, and there's been a lot of encouragement for what we can and can't do.

For a manager, it's not always being used to getting everything that you want, and that's just par for the course - but clearly, I've been well-supported. There's an intention from the board and everybody within the club to try and get the best Rangers squad put together and the best Rangers team on the pitch.

I've got an idea of what my Rangers team needs to look like week in, week out, and how I want my Rangers squad to behave and act day in, day out.

We have similar messaging, similar needs and desires about what we're trying to get, and sometimes it costs money, and sometimes it doesn't. We are on the same page in the sense about the key positions, the type of players that we want to bring in - but everything has got to be done within a reasonable cost. There is the support there, clearly.

Any discussions between you and the club over a deal to sign Lewis Ferguson?

Image: Lewis Ferguson impressed for Scotland at the World Cup

There's been loads of discussions about so many players.

All I want to do is bring players who have a high level, technical level, and ability to play for Rangers.

Obviously, there are a number of players that have been linked with us that do possess that. So, I think it would be wrong for me to speak about any player individually.

I understand it's an obvious link [with Lewis Ferguson], but we have just got to work away and see what we can do and what we can bring into the club.

If it's clear that we can't bring people in, then we move on quickly, but I've got an idea of the players and the types that I want to bring in, and hopefully we can work towards that.

Are you expecting interest in your players from other clubs? For example, Nicolas Raskin.

Image: Nicolas Raskin has impressed for both club and country

Yes, possibly, but these are things that I don't know, that you can't control.

The World Cup is a great stage and obviously Nico [Raskin] has done well.

There will be natural progression for a lot of players. A lot of players aren't going to get guaranteed game time here, and they might be better served going elsewhere to find that, but these discussions are ongoing.

A lot of clubs aren't even back yet because of the World Cup, so sometimes these things can take a bit longer, and there's no doubt we've got good players here who could be of interest.

How excited are you for your first game and for what is possible here at Rangers?

Everything we do from now to then is geared towards that [first match].

Pre-season serves its purpose, games are important just to build that familiarity and continuity, forging those relationships, and understanding what we're looking for.

Pre-season results aren't the most important thing, but what is the most important thing is being as ready as we possibly can be, both physically and tactically for that, and being in the best state possible squad-wise.

We're trying to get as much done on the training pitch, and off the pitch recruitment-wise, so that we can be ready for that game because that game will be a test, there's no two ways about it.

It's a brilliant game, live on Sky Sports and everything that brings with it, so we're looking forward to that.
